#+title: Task: Fix vintage-mode preview chart using stale r0/initial price instead of resolved rate
#+description: IrCurveEditor's and the FX Spot editor's Process/sample-paths chart preview is parameterized from the local editor's r0/gmm_initial_price spin value, which for a vintage-mode config just holds an unused leftover default -- the server resolves the real seed from the vintage observation instead. The chart should be centered on the resolved vintage rate, not the stale local value. Check both IR curve and FX spot editors.

This page documents a [[id:31C868B9-306E-4282-BA8C-07E647021B34][task]] in the [[id:C29FE5A3-61F0-4D2F-BE4F-8A02223EABEF][IR Rates synthetic data: dataset seeding, index cleanup, dual-curve, quoting conventions]] story. It captures the goal, current status, acceptance, and any notes or results.

* Goal

Discovered while manually verifying vintage-aware IR curve seeding
([[id:FC800706-1673-4E48-84C2-22569E836DF5][task]]): =IrCurveEditor='s
sample-paths chart (Process tab) is parameterized directly from
=initialRateSpin_->value()= (=IrCurveEditor.cpp:925=), the editor's
local r0 spin box. For a =price_source=vintage= config, that field
holds an unused leftover/default value -- the server instead resolves
the real starting rate from the vintage market observation at feed
start (=select_vintage_anchor_entry()=). The chart preview therefore
shows sample paths centred on the wrong rate for any vintage-mode
config, which is misleading when a user opens the editor to inspect
or demo a vintage curve.

=FxSpotEditor= has the analogous =gmm_initial_price=/vintage
discriminator (=price_source=/=vintage_source=/=vintage_date=,
mirrored onto IR curves per this story) and likely the same pattern
in its own preview chart -- check it alongside the IR curve editor
rather than fixing IR curves only and leaving FX with the identical
gap.

* Acceptance

- For a =price_source=vintage= config, =IrCurveEditor='s sample-paths
  chart is centred on the resolved vintage rate, not the stale
  =initial_rate= spin value -- either by resolving it client-side (a
  read-only lookup mirroring =select_vintage_anchor_entry()=) or by
  surfacing the already-running feed's resolved rate when one exists.
- =FxSpotEditor='s equivalent preview chart is checked for the same
  gap against =gmm_initial_price= and fixed if present.
- Fixed-mode configs are unaffected -- the chart still reflects the
  typed r0/=gmm_initial_price= exactly, as today.
- Side effect this fixes for free: today there is no way to see the
  server-resolved vintage rate anywhere (=start_ir_curve_feed_response=/
  =list_ir_curve_feed_configs_response= only carry
  success/message/running names, and =resolve_vintage_initial_rate()=
  never logs the value it computes) -- once the chart is centred on
  the resolved rate, opening the editor on a running vintage config is
  enough to visually confirm the process is seeded within the expected
  range, without needing a dedicated status field or log line.
